items.title: Joel Embiid doubtful for Sixers’ NBA Cup showdown vs. Miami Heat
items.text:
Joel Embiid’s illness clearly does not respect the Cup. Sad!
The Sixers are getting dangerously close to full strength, which means in true Sixers fashion, calamity is right around the corner. Lo and behold, Joel Embiid came down with an illness that caused him to miss Monday’s game against the Portland Trail Blazers, and he’s still dealing with it a day later.
Embiid is doubtful to suit up for the Sixers’ NBA Cup game against the Miami Heat on Wednesday, according to the NBA’s injury report . The good news is that aside from Embiid and Ariel Hukporti (Achilles), no one else is even listed for the Sixers. So much for Jaylen Brown’s hamstring injury!
On Miami’s side, two-way signees Tre Donaldson and Vladislav Goldin are out on assignment in the G League, while Myron Gardner is available. The big question mark is Giannis Antetokounmpo, who’s listed as questionable with right groin tendinitis. He missed Miami’s win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday with the same injury, and in his absence, Bam Adebayo messed around and got a triple-double.
If Giannis is able to suit up and Embiid misses the game, the Sixers will have a hell of a time stopping him and Bam down low. None of Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow or Adem Bona have the size to combat the Greek Freak in transition. But if Giannis does sit out, it’ll be more of a fair fight.
The Heat sit atop East Group B with a 2-0 record, while the Sixers are 1-1. If the Heat beat the Sixers, they’ll be all but guaranteed to win the group, as they’ll have the head-to-head tiebreaker over both the Sixers and Cleveland Cavaliers. But if the Embiid-less Sixers can take down the Heat, they’ll have a chance to win Group B as long as the New York Knicks beat the Cavs later Wednesday.
The Sixers have never advanced to the knockout stage of the NBA Cup, but they’ve also never had NBA Cup MVP LeBron James on their roster before this year. And since LeBron is playing on a veteran-minimum contract this year, the prize money for winning the Cup would be more than 10 percent of his salary. That’s assuredly a huge motivation for someone with an estimated net worth of $1.4 billion .
Embiid’s likely absence will give the Sixers a chance to continue experimenting with their backup options as they inch closer to the start of unofficial trade season. They largely went with a Walker-Barlow combo against the Blazers—Bona played only five minutes in his first game back from a cervical spine sprain—but it’s worth keeping an eye on whether the Sixers change that up against the Heat. They should still be in the intel-gathering stage of the season, so the more they mix it up, the better. (Could we even get some brief Tacko Time?)
As someone whose two-year-old is just getting over hand, foot and mouth disease, it’s that time of the year for parents. Here’s hoping the rest of the Sixers stay healthy and Embiid feels better soon.
items.desc: Joel Embiid’s illness clearly does not respect the Cup. Sad!

items.title: ‘It will be my marina.’ Miami Seaquarium’s former leader plots a comeback
items.text:
Former Dolphin Company head Eduardo Albor fights for control in bankruptcy court and to block a Seaquarium deal with developer David Martin.

Eduardo Albor lost control of his dolphin-park empire in 2025 in a bankruptcy, and briefly served time in a Mexican jail as part of his fight to get it back. Now he has a warning for Miami-Dade leaders: Don’t do anything with the Miami Seaquarium without me.
In correspondence with county officials and in an interview with the Miami Herald, the former CEO of the Mexico-based Dolphin Company warns of fatal flaws in Miami-Dade’s plan to let local developer David Martin build a marina, aquarium and entertainment center on the county-owned Seaquarium site. The major flaw alleged by Albor is that control of the Seaquarium’s lease legally still rests with him and that he’ll be vindicated in that view once a judge finally agrees with him.
“The approval for the transfer of the lease — of the rights of the lease agreement — will be null and void,” Albor told the Herald during a video interview this week from his home in Cancun. “If it takes me two or three years and Mr. Martin builds a marina, it will be my marina.”
Albor’s threats are the latest potential roadblock for Martin as he races to secure county approval of his Seaquarium takeover before Dec. 30. That is Martin’s deadline to close a purchase deal of the lease rights from the bankruptcy trustees who now control Albor’s former company.
But while Albor’s legal prophecy would spell doom for Martin’s redevelopment plans, the former CEO’s ambitions are also a selling point for the developer’s accelerated approval timeline. In a recent interview with a Key Biscayne podcast, Martin warned that Albor was waiting in the wings if Miami-Dade commissioners fail to approve Martin’s development deal during a special meeting on Dec. 8.
Albor “has an interest of coming back to this property and operating this property,” Martin told the Anti-Social podcast, hosted by Tony Winton, editor of the Key Biscayne Independent news site. “I’m praying and hoping that we’re able to achieve our goal of getting our Dec. 8th hearing.”
Opponents of Martin’s plan wave off the Albor factor as another effort to rush Miami-Dade commissioners into approving the proposed 99-year lease without considering alternatives for the prime 38 acres of county-owned waterfront.
“Their duty is to explore options for public land,” said Louisa Conway, a Key Biscayne resident and local activist. “They haven’t done that.”
Martin did suffer a setback earlier in the month when a County Commission committee declined to advance his proposed lease package , which the administration of Mayor Daniella Levine Cava released just a day before the Nov. 10 hearing. That set off a scramble by Martin’s lobbying team to circumvent the regular committee process and get the proposal to the full County Commission in early December. Commissioners agreed to schedule the Dec. 8 special meeting to consider Martin’s proposal, which includes a 3% to 5% revenue-sharing provision with Miami-Dade and a pledge to create a free public baywalk on the shoreline of a complex that will include a paid-admission aquarium and a 295-slip marina.
That meeting is set to be the decisive moment for Martin before the County Commission, where he is a top donor to commissioners’ reelection efforts. Last year, commissioners voted unanimously to endorse Martin’s general plan for the Seaquarium property, but formal approval of the lease is still n

items.title: Investigation underway after crash on SB lanes of Palmetto Expressway in Hialeah; 1 hospitalized
items.text:
HIALEAH, FLA. (WSVN) - A Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office deputy has been rushed to the hospital following a crash on the Palmetto Expressway.
Florida Highway Patrol troopers and other law enforcement agencies responded to the southbound lanes of the Palmetto in Hialeah on Tuesday afternoon.
Traffic cameras captured a damaged SUV and a sedan at Northwest 103rd Street along with FHP troopers in the area.
According to Hialeah Fire Rescue, Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units transported the deputy with head injuries to Jackson Memorial Hospital. His condition is unknown.
Please check back on WSVN.com and 7News for more details on this developing story.

items.text:
An officer was airlifted on Tuesday after a crash on the Palmetto Expressway shut down all southbound lanes, police said.
A Miami-Dade deputy was airlifted on Tuesday after a crash on the Palmetto Expressway shut down all southbound lanes, deputies said.
According to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office, the deputy was involved in a traffic crash with another vehicle.
The deputy was airlifted to Jackson Memorial Hospital, while the driver of the vehicle stayed at the scene.
Chopper 6 captured severe traffic on Northwest 103rd Street.
The Florida Highway Patrol is taking over the investigation.

items.title: Miami Beach chief praises cops who confronted duo holding rifles at South Pointe Park
items.text: MIAMI BEACH, Fla. — South Pointe Park had closed at sunset in South Beach. Shortly before 3 a.m. on Halloween, uniformed police officers on foot patrol reported a silver Jeep Grand Cherokee in the parking lot. Officer Christopher Bess, a spokesman for the Miami Beach Police Department, released a statement on Tuesday describing what the officers did after spotting a duo inside the Jeep holding rifles. “Without hesitation, the officers ordered all four occupants to show their hands and subsequently detained them upon the arrival of backup officers,” Bess wrote, according to the statement. Jose Huazano was in the Jeep’s front passenger seat with a stolen loaded handgun and smoking marijuana, according to Bess. Miami Beach Police Chief Wayne A. Jones described Huazano, 20, of Florida City, as “a dangerous individual,” and he praised the officers for being proactive. “I’m confident our officers prevented a tragedy in our city that night,” Jones said in a statement. Huazano’s handgun had been reported stolen in Homestead, according to Bess. “They recovered the loaded handgun, a second handgun from the center console, and two AR-style rifles,” Bess wrote. Miami-Dade County court records showed prosecutors filed a case against Huazano on Nov. 1, and he faced two charges: Third-degree felony grand theft and a misdemeanor for possession of 20 grams or less of cannabis. Huazano was released on a $3,000 bond on Nov. 5, and a judge ordered him to stay away from South Pointe Park. Miami-Dade County Circuit Judge Christine Hernandez was presiding over the case. Local 10 News Senior Assignment Editor Frine Gomez contributed to this report.

items.title: Miami-Dade man accused of pointing camera into neighbor’s bedroom, recording her for at least a month
items.text:
A 60-year-old Miami-Dade County man was arrested after deputies said they found a surveillance camera on his property pointed directly toward a neighbor’s bedroom.

MIAMI-DADE COUNTY, Fla. — A 60-year-old Miami-Dade County man was arrested Monday after deputies with the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said they found a surveillance camera on his property pointed directly toward a neighbor’s bedroom. Leer en español Jail records show Charlie Perez-Acevedo is facing one count of video voyeurism involving a person 19 years and older. According to an arrest report, deputies responded to a “neighbor dispute” around 4:50 p.m. at a located that was redacted. The report states that deputies spoke with a woman identified as the victim, who said she was routinely involved in arguments with Perez-Acevedo, her neighbor. The woman’s age was not disclosed in the report. The woman told deputies that whenever she left her property, Perez-Acevedo used multiple cameras on his property to record her and “yell obscenities at her,” according to the report. She also told deputies that one of the cameras, located on the roof of Perez-Acevedo’s property, had allegedly been recording for approximately one month, deputies said. The camera was “pointed directly toward the interior of her bedroom, where she has a reasonable expectation of privacy,” the report states. Deputies located the camera and said they corroborated the victim’s statement, according to the report. Authorities said Perez-Acevedo was then taken into custody. As of Tuesday afternoon, he remained at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center, where his bond was set at $2,500.
items.desc: A 60-year-old Miami-Dade County man was arrested after deputies said they found a surveillance camera on his property pointed directly toward a neighbor’s bedroom.

items.title: Miami-Dade Transit to operate on Sunday schedule for Thanksgiving
items.text:
Miami-Dade Transit will operate on a modified service schedule on Thursday, Nov. 26, in observance of Thanksgiving Day, the county announced Monday.
Metrobus, Metrorail, Metromover and MetroConnect services will operate on a Sunday schedule throughout the holiday. Regular weekday transit service will resume on Friday, Nov. 27.
Miami-Dade County offices will remain closed on both Thursday and Friday, including the Department of Transportation and Public Works’ administrative, customer service and Special Transportation Services (STS) offices.
However, STS customers will still be able to reserve or cancel trips by calling 305-871-1111.
Transit riders are encouraged to take advantage of digital payment options during the holiday period. Passengers can purchase or reload an EASY Card through the online Transit Store or access available fare options through the GO Miami-Dade Transit, Token Transit, Citymapper, Transit, Moovit and SoFloGo apps.
Riders can also pay their fares directly using a contactless-enabled credit or debit card or a mobile wallet, such as Apple Pay or Google Pay.
Passengers traveling during the Thanksgiving holiday are encouraged to plan their trips in advance and review the modified service schedules on the Miami-Dade County transportation website .

items.title: 1836: Dade County is created
items.desc: Dade County was created on February 4, 1836, named after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River. That same year, Fort Dallas was built and served as a military base during the Second Seminole War.
